register.name: Unified state budget 2026
register.detail: House of Representatives and High Council of State · Agreed April 2026 · 190 billion dinars, about 76% of GDP
register.note: The first unified state budget since 2013; the World Bank gives approximately US$30 billion
register.text: Libya’s first unified state budget since 2013, worth 190 billion dinars, about 76% of GDP, agreed by the House of Representatives and the High Council of State. The World Bank calls it “a landmark step forward” for fiscal discipline: one budget for the public money behind the seven standards.

register.name: Sudan Regional Refugee Response Plan 2026, Libya
register.detail: UNHCR and partners · January to December 2026 · 667,000 people planned for in Libya, 596,000 of them refugees · regional plan of US$1.6 billion
register.note: Libya’s share of the regional plan; UNHCR’s own 2026 requirement for Libya, $51.1 million, was 31% funded at 30 April 2026
register.text: The Libya part of the 2026 Sudan Regional Refugee Response Plan of UNHCR and its partners. Its Libya budget includes $24.7 million for food, $31.1 million for public health and nutrition and $5.7 million for water, sanitation and hygiene, which serve the food, health and water standards.
by: Sudan Regional Refugee Response Plan partners

register.name: Libya Development Trust Fund
register.detail: World Bank Group · Launched December 2023 · with Germany and the United Kingdom
register.note: No amount is stated on the World Bank’s Libya page
register.text: A trust fund, launched with Germany and the United Kingdom, that gives the World Bank Group and its development partners a strategic coordination framework in Libya. By pooling funding and aligning objectives, it supports donor harmonisation, policy dialogue and shared risk management across the work behind the seven standards.

register.name: Transport sector study and strategic plan
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Middle-Income Country Technical Assistance Fund (MIC-TAF) grant · workshop in Tunis, 15 to 17 April 2026 · with the Ministries of Finance and Transportation
register.note: Supplemented by counterpart funding from the Libyan Government
register.text: A grant for a situational and gap analysis of Libya’s transport sector and a strategic plan with prioritised short- to medium-term actions, policy reforms and indicative financing options. It is to identify bankable public and private projects for the roads and ports through which food and goods reach Libyans.

register.name: Strengthening Enabling Business Environment through Public Financial Management Support Project (SEBE-PFM)
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Fund for African Private Sector Assistance grant, supported by Japan · Signed 18 November 2024 · 2024 to 2027
register.note: Signed in the presence of the Minister of Finance and the Embassy of Japan in Libya
register.text: A grant to modernise Libya’s public financial management systems, with an IT infrastructure assessment, a data centre feasibility study and a readiness assessment for an integrated financial management information system. It serves the seven standards through the public money that pays for them.
by: Fund for African Private Sector Assistance

register.name: Waha concessions, extension to 2050
register.detail: National Oil Corporation, TotalEnergies and ConocoPhillips · Signed in Tripoli, 24 January 2026 · new fiscal terms · extended to 31 December 2050
register.note: Held by the NOC (59.16%), TotalEnergies (20.42%) and ConocoPhillips (20.42%); the release states no investment amount
register.text: Extends the Waha concessions, which produce around 370,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day and are operated by Waha Oil Company, wholly owned by the NOC, with new fiscal terms to raise their output. The North Gialo field is expected to add 100,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day, in a nation where oil pays for most of the public money behind the seven standards.

register.name: Misurata Free Zone Port, public–private partnership
register.detail: Misurata Free Zone with Maha Capital Partners (Doha) and Terminal Investment Limited, the port operator of MSC · Release of 20 January 2026
register.note: The amount is in the headline of the Free Zone’s release; the body gives no breakdown
register.text: A partnership to modernise, manage, develop and expand Misurata Free Zone Port, Libya’s main container gateway, with larger container-handling capacity, new equipment and digital systems. The Free Zone calls it the first major public–private partnership in infrastructure outside Libya’s energy sector: trade and jobs beyond oil, for the livelihood standard.

register.name: Resilience to Negative Impacts of Climate-Aggravated Water Scarcity in the Agriculture Sector in Libya (RENEWAL)
register.detail: Adaptation Fund · IFAD · Approved 13 October 2023 · grant of USD 9,995,758 · under implementation
register.note: Listed by the Adaptation Fund as a project under implementation
register.text: An Adaptation Fund grant, implemented by IFAD, to build the resilience of Libya’s farming to climate-aggravated water scarcity. It serves the food and water standards, where 31.6% of Libyans are moderately or severely food insecure.

register.name: Private Sector Development and Entrepreneurship Enhancement Project
register.detail: Reported 30 October 2026 · Grant · Middle-Income Country Technical Assistance Fund · with Expertise France
register.note: Grant for entrepreneurship and small business finance
register.text: Updates Libya’s Private Sector Development Roadmap and Action Plan and trains 50 banking professionals in Islamic finance and lending to small businesses. It is aimed at entrepreneurs, especially women and young people, and serves Livelihood.

register.name: UNHCR Libya, 2026 requirements
register.detail: January to December 2026 · UNHCR’s own requirement for Libya · 31% funded ($15.6M) at 30 April 2026
register.note: UNHCR’s 2026 budget for refugees and asylum seekers in Libya
register.text: Protection, cash, health and shelter help for refugees and asylum seekers in Libya. It serves Food, Health and Shelter.

register.name: UNDP and Japan, human security and resilience in Kufra
register.detail: Signed 28 April 2026 · Japan Supplementary Budget · contribution agreement with UNDP · part of a regional initiative
register.note: Amount not stated in the release
register.text: Supports locally identified priorities in Kufra, in the south-east of Libya. It serves Livelihood and the basic services of the town.

register.name: First public bidding round since 2007
register.detail: Results announced 11 February 2026 · five of 20 blocks awarded · onshore and offshore exploration licences
register.note: No investment amount stated
register.text: Chevron won Sirte S4, Eni with QatarEnergy offshore O1, Repsol with TPAO onshore C3, Repsol with MOL and TPAO an offshore area, and Aiteo Murzuq M1. Exploration revenue funds the state budget that pays for all seven standards.

register.name: Invest4Libya
register.detail: Launched 9 February 2026 · EU funding with support from France · implemented by Expertise France with the Ministry of Finance
register.note: Budget not stated
register.text: Public financial management reform, modern financial markets and growth of green and digital firms. It serves Livelihood.

register.name: Recovery and Development in Libya Facility, Baladiyati III
register.detail: Launched December 2025 · EU grant under the Special Measure in favour of Libya for 2024 · 2025 to 2029 · implemented by AICS
register.note: EU contribution, four years
register.text: Technical help to municipalities and support to central institutions so that local services recover. It serves Water, Health and Education through municipal services.

register.name: WFP Libya country strategic plan, revision 3
register.detail: Approved December 2025 · crisis response revision · plan extended to the end of 2026 · total cost about $158.4M
register.note: Budget increase; beneficiaries rise from about 300,000 to about 514,000
register.text: Food assistance for people in need in Libya, including refugees from Sudan. It serves Food.

register.name: Baladiyati, recovery, stability and socio-economic development
register.detail: Final event 3 September 2025, Tripoli · launched 2018 · EU Emergency Trust Fund for Africa · AICS, UNDP and UNICEF
register.note: Total budget not confirmed at source
register.text: Rebuilt basic services in municipalities across Libya, with a second phase in the south. It served Water, Health, Education and Livelihood.

register.name: bp and NOC, Sarir and Messla redevelopment
register.detail: Signed 7 July 2025 · Memorandum of understanding · Sirte Basin · with studies of unconventional potential
register.note: No investment amount stated
register.text: bp is to evaluate the redevelopment of the Sarir and Messla oilfields and the exploration potential around them. Oil revenue funds the state budget that pays for all seven standards.

register.name: Water Resources Management at Municipal Level in Libya
register.detail: Launched February 2025 · EU grant under the 2023 Special Measure, Water Resources Management Facility · 2025 to 2028 · implemented by AICS
register.note: EU contribution, three years
register.text: Helps municipalities manage scarce water, as part of the Libya–EU Water Resources Management Facility led by GIZ. It serves Water.

register.name: EU4Skills
register.detail: Launched August 2024 · EU funding, co-funded by France · implemented by Expertise France
register.note: EU-funded skills programme
register.text: Gives young Libyans technical skills in digital, green and blue economy and finance work, linking schools, the public sector and firms. It serves Education and Livelihood.

register.name: IFRC network country plan, Libya 2026
register.detail: 2026 · IFRC network funding requirements for Libya
register.note: IFRC network requirement for 2026
register.text: Red Cross and Red Crescent work in Libya on health, disaster response and relief. It serves Health.
by: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Oil
items.label: Output on 21 June 2026, highest since 2013
items.text: Oil and gas bring nearly all exports and government revenue; the NOC aims for 2 million barrels a day.

items.name: The Ground
items.label: Of GDP from natural resource rents, 2021
items.text: What lies under the land already earns; the task is to turn the rent into lasting assets.

items.name: The Grid
items.label: Of citizens with electricity, 2024
items.text: A grid to rebuild and extend, with desert sun to add to it.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2024
items.text: Territory to farm, mine, power and protect.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 26.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: REC
items.text: A recycling enterprise in Derna that collects and recycles debris from demolished buildings, damaged trees and organic waste into reusable resources. It resumed operations after Storm Daniel destroyed its equipment in September 2023, and creates jobs for young Libyans.

items.name: Panda
items.text: A school platform, launched as School Connect with a seed grant from the Tatweer Research Impact Fund, that connects over 10,000 students and their families to thirty schools. It is part of Avanin Technology Education.

items.name: Infinity Libya
items.text: Built what is described as Libya’s first 1 MW solar plant, in Kufra, with the Al-Jouf Free Zone; handed over on 25 May 2025.

items.name: Speetar
items.text: A telehealth platform headquartered in Libya that offers remote consultations, digital health records and referral programmes to people in conflict-affected and remote places. It reports that 724,830 unique individuals have engaged with its digital health services across the countries where it works.

items.name: Al Reaya Al Tebeya for Medical Services
items.text: A Benghazi company, founded in 2023 by a medical doctor, that brings home-based healthcare to people kept from care by distance or limited mobility. It is one of the start-ups supported by an African Development Bank youth entrepreneurship project.

items.name: Tamouh
items.text: A startup in Sebha, founded by a team of female technicians, that offers women a secure, all-female service for device repair and digital maintenance. It creates specialised IT jobs for female engineering graduates in southern Libya.

items.name: Kayan
items.text: A Benghazi platform that connects suppliers, traders and business owners through one application, with remote orders, real-time delivery tracking and transparent prices. It cuts costs for local shops, cafés and restaurants and creates jobs in warehousing, logistics, sourcing and delivery.
